digest.en: Alberta voters just rejected a plan to leave Canada, a decisive check on separatist momentum. Meanwhile, Iranian officials openly call for a nuclear bomb as the regional war stalls. The contrast between domestic consolidation and strategic escalation defines this hour.
digest.hi: रूबियो ने पाकिस्तान को सऊदी अरब में तैनाती की पेशकश करते हुए QUAD और होर्मुज पर बातचीत का रास्ता खोला। इसी दौरान चीन ने DeepSeek पर अमेरिकी बैन को ट्रंप-जिनपिंग समझौते का उल्लंघन करार दिया।

articles.summary: Alberta voters rejected a proposal to begin the independence process by a wide margin. Nearly 1.9 million votes were counted, with 76 percent supporting remaining in Canada. The result delivered a decisive victory for Prime Minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity. articles.title: Ukraine Liberates Dnipropetrovsk Settlements, But Villages Lie In Ruins
articles.summary: Ukrainian forces retaken 26 settlements in the Dnipropetrovsk region. The villages are largely destroyed and uninhabitable. Russian troops are being pushed back, but Ukrainian forces face challenges holding the reclaimed territory under constant drone threat. As Russian troops are pushed back, Ukrainian forces face the challenge of holding the reclaimed territory under constant threat from drones. Ukraine Liberates Dnipropetrovsk Settlements, But Villages Lie In Ruins.

articles.title: With War In Limbo, Influential Iranian Officials Openly Call For A Nuclear Bomb
articles.summary: Influential Iranian officials are openly calling for a nuclear bomb. The death of Ali Khamenei has weakened the political taboo surrounding the weapon. Debate is growing over whether the Islamic republic should abandon its long-standing position against developing nukes. Ali Khamenei's death may not have invalidated his nuclear fatwa, but it has weakened the political taboo surrounding the bomb. Debate is now growing over whether the Islamic republic should abandon its long-standing position against developing nukes.

articles.title: Georgia Faces New Test As Court Weighs Ban On 5 Opposition Parties
articles.summary: Georgia’s Constitutional Court will begin hearings on October 21 regarding a ban on five opposition parties. These parties have collectively won hundreds of thousands of votes. The proceedings mark another critical test for the country’s multiparty democracy, with a final ruling potentially to come later. Georgia’s Constitutional Court will begin hearings on October 21 on a case seeking to ban five opposition parties that together have won hundreds of thousands of votes.

articles.title: Yemen war continues to force families from homes amid hunger and disease
articles.summary: Over 250,000 people have fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the United Nations reported. Access to the southwestern city of Taiz is essentially blocked. This has trapped residents in areas facing severe hunger and disease. The displacement continues to strain local humanitarian resources. More than 250,000 people have now fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the UN said on Tuesday, citing particular concern for those sheltering in the southwestern city of Taiz and the wider governorate, where access is “essentially blocked”.

articles.title: Moldova To Probe Possible Russian Data-Harvesting After RFE/RL Investigation
articles.summary: Moldova launched an investigation into Yandex for allegedly harvesting citizen data. The company reportedly sent personal information to Russian servers instead of the Netherlands. This contradicts previous data storage agreements. The probe follows an investigation by Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty. Moldova has announced an investigation into concerns that Russian tech giant Yandex has been harvesting the personal data of its citizens by sending it directly to servers in Russia rather than storing it in the Netherlands as previously believed.

articles.title: Why Starshield’s slowdown really hurts Ukraine
articles.summary: SpaceX temporarily restricted Starshield satellite internet for Ukrainian forces. This slowdown has raised serious concerns in Kyiv and among its allies. The military-grade service supports critical battlefield communications. The disruption highlights Ukraine’s dependence on external satellite infrastructure. Reports that SpaceX temporarily restricted its satellite internet service for Ukraine’s armed forces have generated serious concern in Kyiv and among the country’s allies.

articles.title: Dhaka’s silence on Saudi executions puts remittances over lives
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia executed two Bangladeshis on October 14, prompting minimal diplomatic reaction from Dhaka. The foreign ministry requested details but assured Riyadh that bilateral relations would remain unaffected. This restrained official response contrasts sharply with widespread public anger on social media, highlighting a preference for remittance stability over immediate political protest. Saudi Arabia executed two Bangladeshis on October 14 but Dhaka’s response was conspicuously restrained.

articles.title: In Delhi or Paris, restoring order cannot replace public trust
articles.summary: Protests often evolve from specific grievances into broader challenges to political authority. When citizens believe their concerns are ignored, demands for correction become questions of accountability. Restoring order alone cannot replace the need for public trust in governance. Protests rarely remain confined to the grievances that first bring people into the streets. When the citizens believe their concerns are being ignored, a grievance over a particular policy or administrative decision can evolve into a broader challenge to the political authority.

articles.title: A growing national crisis and a strategic warning
articles.summary: South Korea's per capita GDP is projected to surpass Japan's by 2027. The International Monetary Fund estimates Korea will reach $49,000. Japan is expected to sit between $37,000 and $38,000. This shift highlights Korea's semiconductor strength. Recent media reports projecting South Korea’s per capita GDP to surpass Japan’s have generated considerable excitement across the regional countries that see Korea as a role model.

articles.title: A Russian Military Satellite Gets Very, Very Close To One Used By Ukraine
articles.summary: A Russian military satellite passed exceptionally close to a Finnish-operated satellite. The Finnish satellite provides intelligence to Ukraine. Officials described the maneuver as concerning and aggressive. They noted it may serve as a signal of hostile intent. Last week, a Russian military satellite came “exceptionally close” to another Finnish-operated satellite that provides intelligence to Ukraine. “It’s concerning and aggressive with potential hostile intent – but I also think cooler heads believe it is signaling on the part of the Russians.”.

He argues the United States will not become a major regional player despite recent diplomatic outreach. Marco Rubio has brought nearly 300 American business representatives to Uzbekistan for a meeting with representatives of the five states of Central Asia. But Daniel N. Rosenblum, a former US ambassador to Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan, cautions that investment faces major obstacles.

articles.title: Funding cuts leave half a million without food assistance
articles.summary: The World Food Programme cut Gaza aid by one third due to funding shortages. The reduction leaves roughly 500,000 people without food assistance as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday. Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third – a move that will affect some 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.

articles.title: Guterres honours Indonesian troops who paid ‘ultimate sacrifice’
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres honored four Indonesian peacekeepers killed in Lebanon. He laid a wreath in their memory and defended the organization's peacekeeping mission during what he described as testing times for global stability. UN Secretary-General António Guterres paid tribute to Indonesian peacekeepers on Monday, laying a wreath in honour of four who recently lost their lives in Lebanon and offering a robust defence of UN peacekeeping in what he called “testing times for peace”.

articles.title: Protecting Earth’s fragile biodiversity takes spotlight at Armenia talks
articles.summary: UN officials in Yerevan warned that biodiversity loss threatens billions of people. The conference emphasized the urgent need for national action. Leaders discussed how protecting ecosystems is critical for future global prosperity and stability. Biodiversity losses continue to upend the lives of billions of people whose future prosperity depends on countries taking urgent action to protect our planet, the top UN official leading talks at the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, said on Monday.

articles.title: Owner or owned? Indonesia’s Chinese battery chain dilemma
articles.summary: Indonesia seeks to transform raw nickel exports into high-value EV batteries. The strategy relies heavily on Chinese investment and technology, raising questions about whether Indonesia controls its supply chain or remains dependent on foreign partners. Indonesia has spent a decade trying to turn its mineral wealth into something more valuable than raw commodity exports. The strategy is ambitious: restrict raw nickel exports, attract investment, build processing capacity and move downstream into electric-vehicle (EV) batteries that will power the next generation of transport and energy storage.

articles.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
articles.summary: Hurricane Trudy weakened to a tropical storm after threatening Mexico's Pacific coast. The system remained 160 kilometers southwest of the shore. Meanwhile, deadly floods in Greece killed one person. The Pacific season saw 22 named systems this year. Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in GreeceIn contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system.

articles.title: Rubio Vows To Keep Pushing For Ukraine Peace, Seeks Deeper US Ties In Central Asia
articles.summary: Marco Rubio stated the United States will continue pushing for a Ukraine peace deal. He warned the conflict risks escalating beyond Russia and Ukraine. The Secretary of State made these remarks while meeting Central Asian officials in Uzbekistan. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington would continue efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine, warning that the conflict risks escalating beyond the two countries as he met with Central Asian officials in Uzbekistan.

articles.title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
articles.summary: China's third-quarter GDP grew by 4.5 percent year-on-year. The figure exceeded previous forecasts. Strong electronics demand boosted industrial output and exports. articles.summary: Three people died in separate float crush incidents during Japanese festivals this weekend. Akihiro Nabae, deputy mayor of Saijo, died after becoming trapped beneath a float. articles.summary: Donald Trump defended waiving planned sanctions against Russia to maintain negotiations. Kyiv and some US lawmakers criticized the move. They argued it sends the wrong message to the Kremlin. The decision drew strong opposition from allies. President Donald Trump defended his decision to waive sweeping sanctions planned against Russia as an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table amid strong criticism from Kyiv and some US lawmakers that it sends the wrong message to the Kremlin.

articles.title: Inside the New York ‘time machine’ racing to save a century of sound and film
articles.summary: Media preservation engineer Rhony Dostaly works in a basement beneath Lincoln Center. He rescues century-old sound and film recordings from decay. His team makes these historical elements available to modern audiences. The project functions as a digital archive for at-risk cultural media. “I tell my kids I work in a time machine,” said Rhony Dostaly. In a basement beneath Lincoln Center, the media preservation engineer rescues moments from the past.

articles.title: Flour sacks turned flood barriers: Gaza faces another winter without safe shelter
articles.summary: Families in the Gaza Strip are bracing for a winter of severe cold and rain that threatens to flood their remaining shelters. Ahmed Al-Omari and others are repurposing flour sacks as makeshift barriers against rising water. These improvised defenses highlight the lack of safe, durable housing in the war-ravaged territory. Residents continue to live in tattered tents and damaged buildings with no reliable protection from the elements. The situation underscores the ongoing humanitarian crisis as winter approaches.

articles.title: How War is Reshaping Iran’s “Axis of Resistance”
articles.summary: Three years of hostilities have fundamentally altered Iran’s regional alliance network. Tehran now relies more heavily on its own military capabilities. While partner states have diminished military utility, Iran maintains its commitment to their protection. This shift reflects a pragmatic adaptation to the changing security environment in the Middle East. Three years of hostilities have transformed Tehran’s network of allies in the Middle East.

articles.title: यूक्रेन ने छुटंकू हथियार से फोड़ी रूस की आंखें, ड्रोन अटैक से कैसे बिगड़ेगा एयर डिफेंस का खेल?
articles.summary: यूक्रेनी सेना ने रूस के S-400 एयर डिफेंस सिस्टम के रडार को ड्रोन हमले में तबाह कर दिया है। इस रडार की कीमत 50 मिलियन डॉलर बताई जा रही है। यह हमला रूसी सेना की हवाई सुरक्षा प्रणाली को तगड़ा झटका देता है। यूक्रेनी सेना ने एक सटीक और खतरनाक ड्रोन हमले में रूस के बेहद आधुनिक और महंगे S-400 एयर डिफेंस सिस्टम के रडार को तबाह कर दिया है.

articles.title: कनाडा से अलग होने का प्रस्ताव अल्बर्टा में खारिज, पीएम कार्नी बोले- लोगों ने कनाडा को चुना
articles.summary: अल्बर्टा में कनाडा से अलगाव के प्रस्ताव को प्रारंभिक परिणामों में खारिज कर दिया गया है। प्रधानमंत्री मार्क कार्नी ने यह फैसला राष्ट्रीय एकता के पक्ष में बताया। उन्होंने कहा कि लोगों ने कनाडा के साथ साझा भविष्य चुना है। ओटावा। कनाडा के प्रधानमंत्री मार्क कार्नी ने अल्बर्टा प्रांत के कनाडा से अलग होने के प्रस्ताव को शुरुआती जनमत संग्रह परिणामों में खारिज किए जाने का स्वागत किया है।

articles.summary: भारत ने एससीओ बैठक में पाकिस्तान को स्पष्ट संदेश दिया। आतंकवादियों को मदद करने वालों को बख्शा नहीं जाएगा। राजनाथ सिंह ने इस कड़ी चेतावनी का ऐलान किया। 'आतंकियों को मदद देने वालों की खैर नहीं': एससीओ बैठक से भारत का पाकिस्तान को दो टूक, और क्या बोले राजनाथ सिंह?

articles.summary: अल्बर्टा के वोटर्स ने कनाडा से अलगाव के प्रस्ताव को ठुकरा दिया। 76 प्रतिशत लोगों ने देश की एकजुटता का समर्थन किया। इससे अलगाववादी आंदोलन पर बड़ा प्रहार हुआ। कनाडा से अलग नहीं होगा अल्बर्टा?: 76 प्रतिशत लोगों ने एकजुटता पर लगाई मुहर, अलगाव का प्रस्ताव।

articles.title: '7.8% से बढ़ रही भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था, वैश्विक वृद्धि में 16% योगदान'; राजनाथ सिंह ने क्या कहा?
articles.summary: राजनाथ सिंह ने ताजिकिस्तान में कहा कि भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था 7.8 प्रतिशत की दर से बढ़ रही है। उन्होंने दावा किया कि भारत वैश्विक वृद्धि में 16 प्रतिशत का योगदान दे रहा है। यह बयान उनकी विदेश यात्रा के दौरान दिया गया। ताजिकिस्तान: '7.8% से बढ़ रही भारत की अर्थव्यवस्था, वैश्विक वृद्धि में 16% योगदान'; राजनाथ सिंह ने क्या कहा?
